summary: Resolves PR #289 hyperscaler-quality blockers by enforcing a flat clean-architecture service taxonomy, removing active customer-facing legacy grouping terminology, preserving .com for public/customer URLs and .dev for internal/developer surfaces, and optimizing the CI-required path so required proof is not duplicated or tied to retired oya-vcs gates.
nonclaims: No live deployment, DNS cutover, or cluster rollout is claimed.
Historical ADR and archived evidence references may retain retired terms only as historical records.
Legacy connector substrate files are not claimed as a product, module, or customer-facing grouping.
Cloud-intelligence rename work was completed by the parallel lane; this PR only performs minimal drift cleanup needed for current gates.

findings: CI-required proof now has one cargo D1-D4 owner; gate run-all owns governance lanes and the hosted required-check mirror, reducing redundant local replay without weakening protection.

Required checks are aligned to the live branch-protection contexts: cargo-fmt, cargo-check, cargo-clippy, cargo-nextest, and oya-pr-review; broader governance lanes remain folded under oya-pr-review until per-lane contexts exist.
Retired grouping wording and public .dev URL gates were rerun after the full verifier and passed across the repo.
Active planning and localization language now uses service/module/libs/kernel/application/infrastructure terminology rather than customer-segment product buckets.
Full ./bin/oya verify --ci-required passed with D1-D7 green and gate run-all 102/102 in /tmp/pr289-oya-verify-ci-required-20260529000418-rerun.log.
Rejected reintroducing retired oya-vcs preflight contexts; ADR-0363 and AGENTS.md make git+PR+Jenkins/governance gates the active substrate.
Branch-protection and hyperscaler-maturity gates now require oya-pr-review as the folded governance review context while preserving direct context matching where available.
The CI-required path avoids running cargo fmt/check/clippy/nextest twice locally; full verification time is now dominated by the single mandatory pass plus governance lanes.
Public/customer surfaces continue to use oyatie.com; internal/developer .dev usage remains scoped to internal surfaces.
Targeted regression tests, live governance gates, full ci-required verification, fmt, diff-check, retired wording, and public .dev scans all passed locally.
PR review status parsing accepts any gate-run-all all-green summary, and cargo status parsing accepts current D-1 through D-4 PASS markers plus legacy markers.
The changes prefer gate-contract alignment and terminology cleanup over adding new dependencies or abstractions.
